claims.text: Menu is dominated by breaded deep-fried items (chicken cutlet, beef cutlet, oyster fry, shrimp fry) sharing fryer oil; no gluten-free handling documented.
Dishes are meat- and seafood-based and sets include miso soup that typically uses fish dashi; no plant-based preparation documented.
Snacks include hishio (a koji/soy-type fermented seasoning) and Nara pickles cured in sake lees; these can involve wheat/barley or soy-derived components and are not confirmed gluten-free.
Among the snacks, sake-lees cream cheese is dairy; pickles and hishio are plant-based but no vegan handling is documented.
Sake is poured by the glass and bottles are visible in the counter fridge, so you can see exactly what you are served and ask staff about each one.

name: 奈良きたまち食堂 イル・ソッリーゾ・デッラ・ファミーリア (Nara Kitamachi Shokudo Il Sorriso Della Fami)

claims.text: Staff ask diners about dislikes and will adjust sauces and ingredients to suit individual tastes, and the menu can be customized on request.
The owner welcomes customer requests and can accommodate dietary preferences or specific dish requests.
As a traditional Japanese kaiseki kitchen, dishes rely on soy sauce and fish dashi, which conventionally contain wheat; no gluten-free sourcing is documented.
Menu is seafood-forward with fish dashi as a base, so vegan diners cannot assume any course is free of animal products.
Completely reservation-only omakase format means the chef may be able to tailor a course to discussed dietary needs if arranged well in advance.

name: 奈良の酒蔵全部呑み うまっしゅ (Nara no Sakagura Zenbu Nomi Umasshu)

claims.text: As a washoku izakaya serving sashimi and handmade dishes, the food is seasoned in the standard Japanese manner, which means wheat-based soy sauce and dashi are integral; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
Most savory dishes are built on fish/seafood and dashi; seasonal vegetable plates are not documented as vegan and likely use bonito or kombu dashi unless requested otherwise.
The local Nara sake poured here is naturally gluten-free, and the small-pour tasting format (50/100/130ml) lets drinkers with dietary limits still enjoy the core sake experience.

name: なら酒蔵なべ (Nara Sakagura Nabe)

claims.text: Menu relies on wheat-based kasu-udon noodles, soy sauce, and sake-lees broths; no gluten-free handling documented.
Standard Japanese izakaya seasonings including soy sauce are used; no wheat-free soy sauce noted.
Signature hot pot broths are made from chicken bones and contain pork, chicken, shrimp, and oysters; shared nabe service makes vegan separation impractical.
An English menu is available, which can help travelers identify dishes and ask about ingredients.

name: 奈良三条カレー 本店 (Nara Sanjo Curry Honten)

claims.text: Japanese-style curry sauce is typically wheat-thickened and the shop documents no gluten-free preparation, so cross-contamination with wheat should be assumed.
Kitchen centers on wagyu beef, seafood, and egg; no separate vegan prep is indicated, so cross-contact with animal products is expected.

name: ならまちパン工房 okage (Naramachi Pan Kobo okage)

claims.text: This is a wheat-flour bakery; all products contain gluten and there is no gluten-free option, so it is unsafe for celiac diners.
No vegan menu is published; enriched breads likely contain dairy and eggs, and there is no stated separation, so vegans should ask about each item.
Ingredients are carefully selected for origin and safety, using all-domestic Japanese wheat and organic yeast.
